summary: Recent coverage focuses on the National Guard's presence in the District, with advocates marking the one-year anniversary of a deployment and arguing that the circumstances underscore the need for statehood. A senator has committed to making D.C. statehood a priority, while civil rights groups say the federal government's role in controlling the District's security situation demonstrates why local autonomy through statehood matters. Without statehood, the District's National Guard answers to the President, not to the officials D.C. residents elect.
